articles.title: Davis Cup 2026: Henry Patten & Neal Skupski win as Great Britain beat Ecuador to reach 'Final Eight'
articles.summary: Great Britain will play in the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after claiming a 4-0 win against Ecuador in London.
articles.body:
Great Britain have reached the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after sealing a 4-0 win in their qualifying tie against Ecuador.

Henry Patten and Neal Skupski booked Britain's ticket to November's 'Final 8' event in Bologna with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles at London's Copper Box Arena.

That gave Britain an unassailable 3-0 lead after wins on Saturday for Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery in the singles , before Harry Wendelken, a late call-up to the team after Cameron Norrie withdrew injured on Friday, wrapped up the best-of-five tie by beating Angel Veliz 6-2 6-3 on his competition debut.

"Three years - it feels like quite a long time," Britain's captain Leon Smith told BBC Sport.

"To do it in three straight rubbers is really good and I'm actually delighted for the guys to look forward to something at the end of the year."

Even against underdogs Ecuador, whose singles players were both ranked outside of the world's top 200, there were doubts if Smith could lead Britain back to the knockout stages given his inexperienced team in London.

Jack Draper ended his difficult season early , while Jan Choinski and Jacob Fearnley were both unavailable through injury.

Smith was then dealt a late blow when British number two Norrie pulled out on Friday after feeling pain in his arm during a practice session.

However, Samuel - after a breakthrough season that has seen him rise from outside the world's top 250 to 95th in the rankings - stepped up on his Davis Cup debut.

Just weeks after winning his first Grand Slam match at the US Open, the 24-year-old overcame nerves and fought back from a set down to beat Andres Andrade 4-6 6-4 6-1.

Fery, meanwhile, was making just his second Davis Cup appearance as the British number one claimed an assured 7-5 6-0 win over Alvaro Guillen Meza.

And with world number one Patten and new US Open champion Skupski to call upon for Sunday's doubles rubber, victory seemed to be well within Britain's grasp.

The pair, despite not playing together on the ATP Tour, combined effortlessly and did not face a single break point against the Ecuadorians.

"We are good friends off the court, which I think always helps, and we spend time with each other when we are on the tour anyway," Patten told BBC Sport.

"[LTA coach] Louis Cayer has created the British system so it's quite easy for Brits to play together - we both have a good idea of what the other player is going to do, where they are going to hit it, where they are going to move to."

The last time Britain made it to the quarter-finals in 2023, they fell to a 2-0 defeat by Novak Djokovic's Serbia, with Norrie and Draper both losing their singles matches.

"When you get to the Final 8 and you play one of the seeded teams, they are extremely strong," Smith said.

"[Italy's Jannik] Sinner could be back playing, [Spain's Carlos] Alcaraz has talked about his commitment to it at the end of the year, but you've got a chance. You try and steal one of the singles, and it goes to the doubles and you've got a good doubles team.

"There's a lot of excitement about it, it brings the team together again."

Three-time defending champions Italy qualified automatically as hosts for the Finals, which will take place in in Bologna from 24 to 29 November.

But the United States, who have won a record 32 Davis Cup titles, will be absent from the quarter-finals for a second successive year after they fell to a 3-2 defeat by the Czech Republic.

Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek won their doubles match to give the Americans a 2-1 lead, but US Open runner-up Ben Shelton lost to Jakub Mensik before Jiri Lehecka sealed the tie for the Czechs with victory over Learner Tien.

South Korea advanced to the knockout stage for the first time on Saturday after beating India 3-1, while Austria joined them with a win over Belgium.

Canada, the 2022 champions, are also through after a 3-1 victory against France, while US Open champion Alexander Zverev won both his singles matches to help Germany to a 3-1 win over Croatia.

Spain are 2-0 up against Chile, with their qualifying tie resuming at 15:00 BST on Sunday.

articles.title: Davis Cup: Great Britain book place in Finals as Neal Skupski and Henry Patten victory over Ecuador
articles.summary: Neal Skupski and Henry Patten sealed Great Britain's place in the Davis Cup Finals in November, with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo; it follows wins for Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel on Saturday, and means GB have reached the last eight for the first time since 2023
articles.body:
After singles victories for Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel on Saturday at London's Copper Box, Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched the tie at the earliest opportunity with a 6-3 6-4 win against Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles rubber.

Britain therefore join three-time defending champions Italy, Canada, Czech Republic, South Korea and Austria in booking their spot for the eight-team event in Bologna.

It is the first time Leon Smith's side have reached the quarter-finals since 2023, when they were beaten by Novak Djokovic's Serbia in Malaga.

Whoever they draw - and as a non-seed they could find themselves up against the likes of Italy or Spain - they will face a much stiffer test than that provided by Ecuador.

The South American outsiders gave their all to the task in the hope of repeating their famous victory in the competition at Wimbledon in 2000 but were outclassed by Smith's men.

Britain are the leading nation in men's doubles and it would have been a huge upset had world No 1 Patten and new US Open champion Skupski not prevailed.

They had played together only once before - Patten's sole previous appearance - in a tie against Canada two years ago but gelled quickly, breaking serve at the first opportunity.

There was a moment of contention on the first point of the second set when umpire Marijana Veljovic ruled that Escobar had hit a volley while leaning across the net, awarding Britain the point.

The Ecuador duo put their anger aside to hold serve but a return winner from Skupski earned them another break in the ninth game, and Patten served out the victory.

"We're very, very happy to get it done in the first match," said Patten. "I think we played a good one."

articles.body:
Última hora del Chile - España de Copa Davis, en directo

Buenas tardes, bienvenidos al segundo día de la eliminatoria de Copa Davis ante Chile. Hoy tendremos en pista a los guerreros que intentarán certificar el pase a la Final a 8 de Bolonia (24-29 de noviembre). Para hacer un breve repaso, Rafa Jódar, Dani Mérida, Jaume Munar, Martín Landaluce y Pedro Martínez, son los seleccionados por David Ferrer para la batalla sobre la tierra de Chile. Por el combinado local, Alejandro Tabilo, Cristian Garín, Tomás Barrios Vera, Matías Soto y Benjamín Pérez lucharán bajo las órdenes de Nicolas Massú, por mantener la racha de 15 años sin ceder en una eliminatoria de Copa Davis como anfitriones. Hoy se disputará el encuentro de dobles.

Jaume Munar y Pedro Martínez buscarán ante Alejandro Tabilo y Tomás Barrios Vera el tercer y definitivo punto para España. Ayer, Dani Mérida tuvo un debut soñado ante Tabilo, con remontada al más puro estilo español incluida. Y posteriormente, Rafa Jódar, el otro debutante del equipo, puso el 2-0 superando con amplia claridad a Garín. Si el dobles no fuera suficiente, los dos madrileños volverán a saltar a pista. Rafa Jódar frente a Tabilo, los primeras espadas de ambos conjuntos, y por si hiciese falta el quinto partido, Dani Mérida intentará batir a Garín. Esperemos que con el dobles sea suficiente...

articles.summary: El madrileño cedió dos juegos, sólo superado por el triple 6-0 de Emilio Sánchez Vicario
articles.body: "No voy a olvidar el debut en la Copa Davis", afirmaba Rafa Jódar tras sumar el segundo punto de la serie ante Chile tras derrotar a Cristian Garín, por 6-0 y 6-2. El madrileño, con 20 años recién cumplidos (los hizo el pasado jueves), se ha convertido ya en historia del tenis español en la máxima competición por países. Sólo Emilio Sánchez Vicario, en el partido contra el argelino Kamel Harrad, de la zona europea de 1984, supera la contundencia del debut de Jódar en una eliminatoria en juego. Emilio firmó un triple 6-0. Carlos Ferrer, en 1953, en otra serie zonal, también perdió dos juegos en su primer partido defendiendo a la selección nacional ante el israelí Mordechai Apel. El resultado en esa ocasión fue de 6-1, 6-1 y 6-0. Rafa sí es el mejor debut con la Armada en este siglo. El mejor estreno estaba en manos de Juan Carlos Ferrero, que cedió seis juegos ante Yevgeny Kafelnikov en la primera ronda del Grupo Mundial 2002. Juanqui se impuso por un triple 6-2.

articles.standfirst: La pareja española tuvo bola de doble rosco ante Tabilo y Barrios y sentencia a Chile
articles.summary: La pareja española tuvo bola de doble rosco ante Tabilo y Barrios y sentencia a Chile
articles.body: Los 15 años de imbatibilidad de Chile como local y las 12 eliminatorias ganadas por Nicolás Massú en su banquillo ya son historia. El Parque Deportivo Estadio Nacional se preveía una caldera y se convirtió en un balneario en el que se paseó la selección española de la Copa Davis. Dani Mérida, Rafa Jódar y el dobles formado por Jaume Munar y Pedro Martínez han firmado un contundente 0-3 como visitantes. Por no haber no había ni la grada llena porque los aficionados locales ya intuían lo que iba a pasar después del resultado parcial de la primera jornada. España no es Paraguay, Perú, México, Venezuela, República Dominicana, Colombia, Ecuador, Eslovaquia, Kazajistán, Luxemburgo o una Serbia sin Novak Djokovic. Al rosco el sábado de Jódar ante Cristian Garín le siguió el 6-0 y 6-2 de Munar y Martínez ante Alejandro Tabilo y Tomás Barrios. El dúo español se mantiene invicto en la máxima competición por países. Tres partidos y otras tantas victorias. Y eso que no se juntaban a mitad de pista desde el Open de Australia en el mes de enero. La ruidosa hinchada chilena empezó como un campo neutral porque sus jugadores no les dieron razones de creer. El ruido llegó con tres juegos ganados por Tabilo y Barrios después de que Jaume y Pedro disfrutaran de una bola de doble 6-0. "El mérito es de los jugadores, que son muy buenos", decía Ferrer a los micrófonos de Movistar +. "Creo que hemos hecho un partidazo, lo que se ve en la pista es el ambiente que hay fuera", decía Munar. "Ellos estaban encogidos por el resultado y se han soltado después", comentaba Martínez. Martín Landaluce, a sus 20 años, se unió a la fiesta ganando el cuarto punto ante Matías Soto, por 6-2 y 6-3. El conjunto español conocerá este martes el cuadro de la fase final de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Como cabeza de serie evitará a los otros favoritos en los cuartos.

articles.body: La selección nacional de la Copa Davis, que ha logrado este domingo su pase a la fase final de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre), conocerá este martes su camino hacia la séptima Ensaladera de su historia. La Alemania de Alexander Zverev también partirá entre las favoritas y el cuarto será la República Checa. Los italianos, vigentes campeones, además de anfitriones, irán por la parte alta del cuadro. Han levantado las últimas tres coronas en la máxima competición por países. El primer rival de España saldrá entre Canadá, Gran Bretaña, Corea del Sur y Austria. Cuatro de las ocho primeras selecciones del ranking no estarán en Bolonia: Bélgica (4), Estados Unidos (5), Francia (6) y Australia (8).

articles.title: "I was close to giving up": Aryna Sabalenka opens up on how she nearly ended her career in tennis amid the 2026 US Open loss
articles.summary: International Sports News: Aryna Sabalenka is easily one of the most talented athletes in the world even as she suffered a loss in the 2026 US Open. The 28 year old tennis star .
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka is easily one of the most talented athletes in the world even as she suffered a loss in the 2026 US Open. The 28 year old tennis star is now gearing up for the China Open which begins in the next 10 days. But it seems, at one point in her life, Aryna Sabalenka wanted to give up on her stellar career.Aryna Sabalenka reflects on how she wanted to end her career in tennis but it is her family that kept her going through all the challenging daysA few months ago, in an interview with Vogue, the 4 Grand Slams title winner Aryna Sabalenka reflected on the challenges she faced in her life as she said, “There was a period when I was probably nine when I was close to giving up. But I saw how proud my dad was of me, and I didn’t want to disappoint him. And then I fell in love again with the sport, much more than before.”The 28 year old Belarusian professional tennis star added, “After I lost my father, it’s always been my goal to put our family name in the history of tennis…”Aryna Sabalenka continued, “Every time I see my name on that trophy, I’m so proud of myself, I’m proud of my family that they never gave up on my dream and that they were doing everything they could to keep me going.”While Aryna Sabalenka has had a successful career in tennis, she has often opened up about the challenges her family faced while raising her and her siblings.To make things worse, when the tennis star was just 13 years old, Aryna Sabalenka’s parents faced financial issues but they never let their children know what was happening.Despite the secrecy, Aryna Sabalenka has often spoken about how she and her siblings always knew the financial challenges their family was facing even though their parents tried to keep things private.Aryna Sabalenka reflects on witnessing her father’s death and how he could have been saved Later, in 2019, Aryna Sabalenka ended up losing her father to sepsis and she has often reflected on how he became a victim of medical negligence after he was refused to be taken to the hospital at the right time by paramedics.In the same interview with Vogue, the 4 Grand Slams title winner Aryna Sabalenka reflected on how she was training in Minsk during the November offseason when her father passed away.She said, “I was like, let me f–king carry him to the hospital myself if the ambulance isn’t taking him…They took him on the third day, and it was too late.”Despite the challenges she faced, Aryna Sabalenka kept her focus on her career and is one of the greatest athletes in the world today.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Zverev critica la Final a 8 de Bolonia: "La Copa Davis es historia y no dinero”
articles.standfirst: El alemán reclama el regreso de las eliminatorias a cinco partido en casa o fuera y alejado de la sede neutral de los últimos años
articles.summary: El alemán reclama el regreso de las eliminatorias a cinco partido en casa o fuera y alejado de la sede neutral de los últimos años
articles.body: Alexander Zverev no es alguien que habitualmente se muerda la lengua a la hora de decir lo que piensa y la Copa Davis no ha sido una excepción. El reciente ganador del US Open hizo un enorme esfuerzo para representar a su país en la eliminatoria frente a Croacia disputada en Halle y ganó sus dos puntos individuales para meter a Alemania en la Final a 8 de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Zverev se emocionó con el ambiente vivido en el Heristo Arena de Halle y acabó mostrando una gran bandera alemana en medio de la pista, rememorando el ambiente clásico de la Davis. Y eso es precisamente lo que echa de menos. “Lo que jugaremos en Bolonia dentro de unos meses no tiene nada que ver con la Copa Davis. Esta atmósfera era la verdadera Copa Davis. No todo torneo tiene que girar alrededor del dinero. La Copa Davis es historia y no dinero”, dijo Sascha tras su segunda y definitiva victoria que daba a Alemania el tercer punto que necesitaba para imponerse por 3-1 a los croatas. Zverev ya estuvo el año pasado en la Final a 8 de Bolonia tras varios años de ausencia, cayendo en semifinales ante España pese a ganar su partido ante Munar. La Davis es uno de los pocos títulos que le faltan a un tenista que ya sido campeón olímpico y doble ganador de la ATP Finals, más allá de sus victorias de este año en Roland Garros y el US Open. La segunda ronda de los clasificatorios para la Final a 8 de Bolonia se ha jugado con el formato clásico, en casa de uno de los contendientes y al mejor de cinco partidos. El formato cambió en 2019, siendo España el primer campeón al derrotar a Canadá en la final disputada En la Caja Mágica de Madrid. Alemania no gana el título desde 1993, cuando derrotó por 4-1 a Australia en Düsseldorf con Michael Stich como principal estilete. Era su tercer entorchado.

articles.title: In 2014, Naomi Osaka’s family faced eviction while she was still chasing her tennis breakthrough; a year later, she had earned just $6,290 in six months before becoming a four-time Grand Slam champion
articles.summary: International Sports News: Naomi Osaka was 16 when her family received an eviction notice on their Florida condominium. Her professional tennis career was still developing, and .
articles.body: Naomi Osaka was 16 when her family received an eviction notice on their Florida condominium. Her professional tennis career was still developing, and her earnings were nowhere near enough to provide financial security. A year later, she had earned just $6,290 during the first six months of 2015, a figure that looks very different against the career she would eventually build.More than a decade later, Osaka has four Grand Slam singles titles, a former world No. 1 ranking and a career that stretches beyond tennis into investments, sports ownership, media and fashion.The family gamble behind the Stanford breakthroughOsaka’s professional journey began with her father, Leonard François, who coached Naomi and her older sister Mari. François was inspired by Richard Williams and chose to develop his daughters outside the traditional American junior tennis system. The family had moved from Japan to the United States when Naomi was three and eventually settled in Florida.The financial pressure became particularly difficult in 2014. According to details from Ben Rothenberg’s biography of Osaka reported by Tennis.com, the family received an eviction notice on their Pembroke Pines condominium about a month before Naomi entered qualifying at the Bank of the West Classic in Stanford. They were given six weeks to leave, at a time when the sisters’ tennis careers had not produced enough income to cover the family’s expenses.The Stanford tournament soon gave Osaka an opportunity to change that picture. The 16-year-old qualified for the main draw and faced Samantha Stosur, the 2011 US Open champion and a former world No. 4. Osaka defeated Stosur in three sets, earning $10,000 in prize money and attracting greater attention from sponsors.Her finances were still modest after the breakthrough. According to the same biography details, Osaka earned only $6,290 during the first six months of 2015, while Mari earned $2,160 during the same period. Osaka was still climbing the professional rankings, with the Grand Slam titles and commercial success that would eventually transform her career still ahead of her.The Grand Slam years changed the scaleOsaka’s rise accelerated in 2018 when she won her first WTA title at Indian Wells. Later that year, she reached the US Open final and defeated Serena Williams 6-2, 6-4 to claim her first Grand Slam singles championship.The following January brought another major breakthrough. Osaka defeated Petra Kvitova in the 2019 Australian Open final to win her second consecutive Grand Slam title and became the first Japanese player to reach No. 1 in the WTA rankings. She was 21 years and 104 days old when she reached the top position.Naomi Osaka added another US Open title in 2020 and another Australian Open championship in 2021, taking her Grand Slam total to four. Her success also transformed her commercial profile. Forbes estimated that she earned $37.4 million between June 2019 and June 2020, including $34 million from endorsements and $3.4 million in prize money, making her the highest-paid female athlete on its list for that period.That was a dramatic change from the $6,290 she had earned during the first half of 2015. Osaka had gone from a teenager trying to establish herself on the professional circuit to an athlete whose name carried major commercial value, and she began using that platform to pursue opportunities beyond sponsorships.From endorsements to investments and ownershipOsaka’s business career began taking a different shape as she started investing in companies and taking ownership positions. In 2019, she invested in BodyArmor and received an equity stake in the sports drink company. Coca-Cola acquired the remaining 85% of BodyArmor in 2021 in a deal that valued the company at $5.6 billion.She also moved into sports ownership. In 2021, Osaka became an investor in the North Carolina Courage of the National Women’s Soccer League. When the club announced the investment, she spoke about the women who had supported her while she was growing up and connected her decision to opportunities for women in sport.“The women who have invested in me growing up made me who I am today,” Osaka said in the club’s announcement. She also said she wanted to invest in women who could become role models and leaders.Her own ventures added another dimension. Osaka launched KINLÒ in 2021, a skincare and suncare brand developed with melanated skin in mind. In 2022, she and Stuart Duguid launched Hana Kuma, a media company focused on stories and creators from different backgrounds. The company later raised $5 million as it expanded its work across entertainment and culture.Osaka has also invested in other consumer businesses. In 2024, she participated in funding rounds involving companies including Pressed Roots and W, adding more ventures to a portfolio that has continued to grow alongside her tennis career.A new chapter in 2026Osaka’s business interests have continued to expand in 2026, with fashion becoming one of her newest areas of focus. In August, she unveiled a prototype for a luxury leather-goods project with designer Mike Cherman at Uncharted’s Fame to Fortune Summit. Osaka described the project as her “biggest dream” outside tennis while explaining how her success in the sport had created opportunities to invest and work with people who could help develop her ideas.Her professional setup also changed at the beginning of the year. Osaka left Evolve, the sports agency she had co-founded with Duguid, at the end of 2025 and returned to IMG for tennis representation in January 2026.On the court, Osaka remains an active professional in 2026, with the WTA listing four Grand Slam titles and a career-high No. 1 ranking. Her return to major competition has added another chapter to a career that has included a rapid rise, a period away from the tour and a return to professional tennis after becoming a mother.The contrast with her early years is difficult to miss. In 2014, her family was dealing with an eviction notice while Osaka was still searching for her first major breakthrough. In the first six months of 2015, she had earned $6,290. Within a few years, her annual earnings were being measured in tens of millions of dollars, while her career expanded into investments, ownership and businesses of her own.In 2026, Osaka is still competing as a Grand Slam champion, but tennis is now only one part of her professional life. articles.title: Billie Jean King Cup: Great Britain prepare for tough Czech Republic test
articles.summary: Great Britain face the Czech Republic at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals on Tuesday - and know full well the size of the challenge facing them.
articles.body:
"It's best not to underestimate us," says a defiant Harriet Dart.

But Great Britain's Billie Jean King Cup squad know full well the enormity of the challenge that awaits them.

On Tuesday, the tight-knit British team - Dart, Katie Boulter, Sonay Kartal, Mika Stojsavljevic and Jodie Burrage - take on the Czech Republic in their BJK Cup quarter-final in Shenzhen, China.

GB have reached the semi-finals in three of the past four seasons, but in the Czechs they face the 11-time champions and an eye-watering line-up - the only team boasting two top-10 players at the Finals tournament.

In Linda Noskova and Karolina Muchova, they have the current Wimbledon champion and her beaten opponent from this summer's all-Czech final.

While Marie Bouzkova has not yet hit such heights in reaching a major final, the 28-year-old has won two WTA titles this year, including on the Nottingham grass, and team-mate Sara Bejlek, 20, has enjoyed a breakthrough season featuring a first title and victories against the likes of Aryna Sabalenka and Madison Keys.

In doubles, Bouzkova and Noskova teamed up to triumph in Cincinnati in August, though Katerina Siniakova is likely to feature in the BJK Cup as the current top-ranked women's doubles player with 12 Grand Slams to her name.

All five members of the Czech team are ranked higher in the singles rankings than any of the British squad.

"I think naturally we are definite underdogs," Boulter, the current world number 54, told BBC Sport.

"We are the ones that are going to have to make something happen, something special. But that being said, a lot of pressure is on them, and we've seen in this tournament before that people can make upsets, and I think that's what we'll be looking to do.

"I think we have no pressure ourselves, and we're just going to go out there with no expectations."

The tie will be shown on the BBC Sport website and app and on BBC iPlayer, with coverage beginning from 10:00 BST.

Billie Jean King Cup: Czech Republic v Great Britain

Coverage from 10:00 BST on BBC Sport website and app and BBC iPlayer

By her own reckoning, the 2026 season has brought "an improvement" for Boulter, winning her fourth WTA title in Ostrava and beating new world number one Elena Rybakina at Queen's in a year in which the Kazakh won the Australian and US Open crowns.

But the British number one has repeatedly come unstuck against Czech players.

Boulter lost 6-3 7-5 to Muchova in Miami back in March but fell to a more emphatic defeat to her in the US Open second round earlier this month, winning just one game in a "bad day at the office".

She faced Noskova in Cincinnati in August and lost 6-3 6-3, but Boulter can take confidence from the fact she beat the Czech in straight sets in Osaka in October 2025.

"They are both incredible players, both extremely good at what they do," Boulter, 30, said.

"They have been in places that I've never been before. So I think for me, it's about taking it to them.

"Their base level is so high, you can't play the same way that you would normally play if you were to play someone ranked a lot lower.

"I think you have to give them respect, but also play the ball that's coming at you at the same time. That's my challenge, to focus on the ball coming at me and try and impose my own game.

"I think there are ways I'm going to try and win points, and that's through what I'm doing, not what they're doing."

Dart, who lost 6-2 6-2 to Bouzkova in the US Open second round, said: "I think even though the match-up on paper here is pretty rough for us, at the same time I know how well this team can play.

"We have strong belief within ourselves and within our own team that we can do well in this competition."

Great Britain qualified for Shenzhen - their fourth BJK Cup Finals in five years - by shocking Australia in Melbourne in April.

Boulter and Kartal were among a list of absentees from that squad - including Emma Raducanu, who is again missing through injury - but the pair's return to the line-up strengthens captain Anne Keothavong's side.

Should they pull off an upset and beat the Czechs, GB would next play the winner of the quarter-final between Kazakhstan - who are without Rybakina - and Spain on Friday.

"I think pressure is a privilege, isn't it? I think whoever you're drawn against in this competition, particularly when you've made it through to the Finals, there are no easy matches," said Keothavong.

"We've seen over the years how people are able to rise to the occasion when they represent their nation. I've seen it from the players here beside me.

articles.title: El Ferrero Challenger de Villena tendrá un cuadro de primer nivel para su novena edición
articles.standfirst: Todos los jugadores inscritos están en el 'top200' y Darwin Blanch entra con una invitación de Next Gen
articles.summary: Todos los jugadores inscritos están en el 'top200' y Darwin Blanch entra con una invitación de Next Gen
articles.body: El Ferrero & Forty Challenger celebrará del 4 al 11 de octubre, en Villena (Alicante), su novena edición. El torneo, de categoría 100, se consolida como el más importante que se disputa en España sobre superficie dura. Una de las grandes novedades de esta edición es la incorporación de FORTY Group como socio estratégico, aportando un nuevo impulso al proyecto e integrando el mejor tenis internacional con una propuesta que combina gastronomía, cultura, ocio, actividades familiares y encuentros empresariales. El torneo tendrá una bolsa en premios de más de 160.000 euros. Por lo que hace referencia a la puntuación en el ranking ATP, el título vale 100 puntos, que son los que se suman para alcanzar las semifinales de un Open 250 del calendario tenístico. Pablo Carreño es el vigente campeón de un certamen que tiene en su palmarés a Carlos Alcaraz. La lista de jugadores inscritos ha cerrado en el puesto 184 con el checo Jam Kumstat. Entre los nombres más destacados están Pedro Martínez, componente del equipo español de la Copa Davis; Dino Prizmic, número 1 de Croacia en la reciente eliminatoria en Alemania de la máxima competición por países; o Pablo Llamas, otra promesa de la Armada que llama a las puertas del 'top100'. Darwin Blanch, una de las grandes esperanzas del tenis estadounidense y formado en la prestigiosa Ferrero Tennis Academy, tiene un lugar asegurado en el cuadro de 32 participantes gracias a la invitación de la Next Gen Acelerator. "Organizar este torneo es un motivo de orgullo para nosotros", señala Juan Carlos Ferrero, número uno del mundo en 2003 y que durante el torneo presentará el libro “Mentalidad Ganadora” sobre sus vivencias en el circuito. "Más allá del nivel deportivo, representa el compromiso y la pasión que sentimos por el tenis. Queremos que todos los jugadores y aficionados vivan una experiencia inolvidable”, comenta. El torneo abrirá sus puertas el domingo 4 de octubre con la fase previa y una jornada especial de puertas abiertas. Desde el lunes, la acción no se detiene y es que habrá más cosas, además de tenis, en la Ferrero Tennis Academy de Villena.

articles.title: Why world No.1 Sinner cannot afford to skip the Asian swing despite his injury, especially after US Open withdrawal
articles.summary: International Sports News: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner faces a tough choice between returning to competitive play during the challenging Asian swing or waiting for the indoor season to avoid injury setbacks. His recent US Open withdrawal due to a knee issue complicates his ranking and preparation for the upcoming ATP Finals in Turin.
articles.body: Jannik Sinner has not played a match since lifting the Wimbledon trophy on July 12, and his absence from the US Open has now turned the next few weeks into a careful balancing act. The world No. 1 can return in Asia, where he has already experienced problems in difficult conditions, or wait for the indoor season and build towards the ATP Finals in Turin. Either route carries a cost, with Alexander Zverev waiting for an opportunity.Sinner's comeback could be delayed until ViennaSinner's last appearance came at Wimbledon on July 12, when he won the title, and more than two months have now passed without another competitive match.The Italian was forced to withdraw from the 2026 US Open before the tournament because of a right knee issue, which had also kept him out of the preceding North American hard-court events in Montreal and Cincinnati. It was the first Grand Slam tournament Sinner had missed since making his Flushing Meadows debut in 2019.His eventual return therefore remains uncertain, and former ATP professional Stefano Pescosolido believes Sinner could choose to miss the Asian swing altogether rather than immediately expose himself to the heat and humidity of Beijing and Shanghai.“I think he's a little more careful from a physical standpoint. He wants to avoid relapses,” Pescosolido told Tuttosport.“The Slams are his main goal, and I imagine he wants to be at his best next year to try to win as many as possible. There are two options: Beijing and Shanghai, or starting with the indoor tournaments.”The concern is not simply the knee problem that forced Sinner out of the US Open.Sinner has a documented history of struggling physically in hot conditions, including at the Australian Open over the past two years and at European events, while his most dramatic episode came at the French Open this year.Sinner was leading Juan Manuel Cerundolo and was one game away from victory in their second-round match at Roland Garros when he suffered severe cramps and a complete loss of energy, leaving him unable to mount a meaningful response.That collapse came after Sinner had played all five Masters 1000 tournaments in the build-up to Paris, with the accumulated workload becoming part of the discussion around his physical condition.China has presented similar problems.At the Shanghai Masters last year, Sinner struggled with the humidity and eventually retired during his match against Tallon Griekspoor, despite that contest being played in a night session.Pescosolido therefore believes the indoor season could offer a more controlled route back.“Last year, at the ATP 1000 tournament in China, the conditions were difficult and he withdrew due to cramps,” Pescosolido said. “He could skip the Asian trip and return from Vienna, to be ready for the ATP Finals, in order to best plan for the following year.”That would put the Erste Bank Open in Vienna at the centre of Sinner's potential comeback.The ATP 500 indoor hard-court tournament is scheduled for October 26 to November 1, 2026, at Vienna's Wiener Stadthalle, and Sinner has a particularly strong connection with the event after winning the title in 2023 and 2025.Returning indoors would also remove the heat and humidity that have contributed to some of his recent physical difficulties, while giving him competitive matches before the season-ending championship in Turin.Skipping China could put Sinner's No. 1 ranking under pressureThe problem with protecting his body is that Sinner's ranking does not stop moving simply because he is not playing.He has already qualified for the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals, which will be held at the Inalpi Arena in Turin from November 15 to November 22, but the Italian will have to consider what happens to his ranking if he remains away from the Asian tournaments.Sinner is the defending champion in Beijing, meaning that if he chooses not to play there, he would lose 500 ranking points. That would reduce his advantage over Alexander Zverev, even if the German also decided to skip the tournament.Zverev has relatively few points to defend from last year's Asian swing and could therefore make up further ground by going deep in Shanghai, particularly given the form he has shown after winning two Grand Slam titles this year.The German also has points to defend later in the indoor season, having reached the Vienna final and the Paris Masters semi-finals last year, but a strong Asian swing would still give him an opportunity to close the gap before Sinner returns.That creates a difficult calculation for Sinner.Playing in Beijing and Shanghai would allow him to defend ranking points and prevent Zverev from gaining ground, but it would also mean returning from a knee problem in the same type of hot and humid conditions that have previously caused him physical difficulties.Waiting until Vienna would give him an indoor environment and more time to prepare, but it would leave Zverev with an extended opportunity to challenge his position at the top of the rankings.Turin is the target Sinner has to protectThe wider objective is the Nitto ATP Finals, where Sinner will defend his title in front of his home crowd.The tournament brings together the top eight singles players and top eight doubles teams at the end of the ATP season, with this year's edition scheduled for November 15-22 in Turin.Sinner's indoor record makes a return through Vienna particularly attractive if he decides that avoiding Asia is the better option. He has won 10 titles from 12 indoor finals, including his two Vienna championships, giving him a strong competitive base on which to rebuild his rhythm before Turin.The timing also allows Sinner to think beyond the final weeks of 2026.There is, however, a reason Sinner may find the decision difficult even beyond the rankings.He has won two titles in Beijing and one in Shanghai during his career, meaning the Asian swing has been a productive part of his schedule rather than an unwanted detour. Skipping both tournaments would therefore mean giving up opportunities to compete in places where he has already enjoyed significant success.For now, the choice is between returning sooner in conditions that have previously tested him physically or waiting for the indoor courts of Vienna, where he has already proved himself twice.Either way, Sinner's next tournament will carry more weight than a routine return from injury, because the world No. 1 is trying to protect both his body and his position at the top before the season reaches its final stretch in Turin.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El maratón de Kaitlin Quevedo: de campeona en Sao Paulo a las finales de la Billie Jean King Cup
articles.standfirst: La española, reciente ganadora de su primer título WTA, viajará a Shenzhen para juntarse con el equipo español de cara a la eliminatoria de cuartos de final ante Kazajistán
articles.summary: La española, reciente ganadora de su primer título WTA, viajará a Shenzhen para juntarse con el equipo español de cara a la eliminatoria de cuartos de final ante Kazajistán
articles.body: Kaitlin Quevedo se ha coronado por primera vez en Sao Paulo. La tenista formada en Florida ha derrotado a la argentina Nadia Podoroska (200 del mundo), la verdugo de Paula Badosa, por 4-6, 6-4 y 6-2 para poner el broche de oro a una semana mágica y así levantar su primer certamen. Con 20 años y siete meses, se trata de la jugadora española más joven en levantar un título profesional desde que Garbiñe Muguruza (20 años y tres meses) estrenara su palmarés en Hobart 2014. Desde 2021 no hay dos tenistas españolas ganadoras de torneos WTA la misma temporada. Ese año lo lograron Paula Badosa, Garbiñe Muguruza y Sara Sorribes. Esta temporada, Cristina Bucsa en Mérida y Quevedo en Sao Paulo han cambiado la historia. Tres roturas de saque, dos de ellas de la argentina, abrieron el partido por el título. La española recuperó una de ellas en el cuarto juego, cortando la sangría inicial de la argentina. El primer set lo cerró Podoroska a base de defender su servicio. Para la 200 del mundo también era su primera final profesional. En la segunda manga, la insistencia de Quevedo tuvo premio. 'Break' con 5-4 a favor para empatar la final. La española tenía una misión, llegar a Shenzhen como campeona WTA. Y así fue. Un 6-2 en la manga definitiva la convirtió en la vigésima jugadora española en levantar un título profesional. Pero Quevedo no tendrá mucho tiempo para celebraciones. El miércoles 23, el equipo capitaneado por Carla Suárez Navarro disputará la eliminatoria de cuartos de final de la Billie Jean King Cup ante Kazajistán. Lo que ajusta de sobremanera los tiempos de la joven de 20 años, que en un principio tendría que haber disputado la final del WTA brasileño el domingo. Las fuertes lluvias sobre la Quadra Central Maria Esther Bueno lo impidieron. Esta situación afecta a la planificación del equipo español. La tenista canaria, segunda espada de la plantilla, tiene previsto aterrizar en China poco antes del inicio de la serie (11:00 h España), lo que le imposibilita ser partícipe del duelo ante las kazajas, que no contarán con la ayuda de la número 1 del mundo, Elena Rybakina. Hasta el momento, solo tres tenistas se han podido ejercitar sobre la pista central Shenzhen Bay Sports Centre Arena. Esta mañana lo hicieron Jessica Bouzas y Marina Bassols, por la tarde, Sara Sorribes entrenó dobles. Cristina Bucsa, la número uno española, aterriza hoy en la ciudad asiática, tras su título junto a Nicole Melichar en Guadalajara, para ponerse a las ordenes de Carla Suárez.

articles.title: Fonseca no jugará la gira asiática para cuidar su salud física y mental
articles.standfirst: El brasileño reconoce "haber hecho un gran esfuerzo jugando la Copa Davis" y se dará un descanso de las pistas
articles.summary: El brasileño reconoce "haber hecho un gran esfuerzo jugando la Copa Davis" y se dará un descanso de las pistas
articles.body: Joao Fonseca está pasando por la temporada más dura de su carrera. Tras bajarse del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati y el US Open por una lesión abdominal, el joven brasileño tampoco estará presente en la gira asiática, que dará comienzo el próximo miércoles 23 de septiembre en Chengdu y Hangzhou. Fonseca ha subido un comunicado en su cuenta de Instagram en el que anuncia su complicada situación a nivel físico y mental: "Hola a todos. Quería compartir algo con vosotros. El 2026 ha sido un año muy difícil para mí. Además de las exigencias propias de la profesión, una serie de lesiones me han dejado fuera de torneos importantes y me han impedido jugar como me gustaría", empieza el número 28 del ranking ATP. "Sé que esto forma parte de la vida de un deportista, pero aun así resulta frustrante. Hice un gran esfuerzo por volver y representar a Brasil en la Copa Davis, pero todavía necesito más tiempo. He hablado mucho con mi equipo y hemos llegado a la conclusión de que lo mejor ahora es escuchar a mi cuerpo, dar un descanso a mi mente y a mi físico, y no participar en la gira asiática. Muchas gracias a todos por el apoyo. ¡Nos vemos pronto!", concluyó el jugador brasileño, que no disputará el ATP 500 de Tokio, como estaba planeado, ni el Masters 1000 de Shanghái. El esfuerzo de Joao fue suficiente para imponerse al suizo Dominic Stricker y ayudar a su país a llevarse la eliminatoria por 3-1 ante Suiza. Esto hará que Brasil dispute los clasificatorios a la Final a 8 de la Copa Davis en 2027.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner now has a golden opportunity to achieve historic feat only three players have ever managed
articles.summary: It will certainly have been frustrating for Jannik Sinner to watch the US Open unfold from home, as it was probably a fairly comfortable tournament...
articles.body:
It will certainly have been frustrating for Jannik Sinner to watch the US Open unfold from home, as it was probably a fairly comfortable tournament for him to win had he been fit.

With Carlos Alcaraz not quite at 100% and Novak Djokovic bowing out in the first round, the draw in New York was wide open.

It was ultimately Alexander Zverev who seized the moment, with the German defeating Ben Shelton in the final to capture his first US Open title and second Grand Slam overall.

Sinner may be finishing the season with fewer majors than his fans had expected, but he still has plenty to play for in 2026, including a historic feat.

Jannik Sinner's chance to make history at the ATP Finals

Sinner has four title defences to take care of between now and the end of the season, the first of which comes at the China Open.

From there, he will defend his crowns at the Vienna Open and the Paris Masters, before competing at the ATP Finals.

Sinner has not lost a match at the ATP Finals since the 2023 edition of the year-end tournament, where he fell in the final to Novak Djokovic.

Since then, he has gone back-to-back at the ATP Finals without dropping a set.

Now, Sinner is bidding to become just the fourth player in men's tennis history to win the ATP Finals for a third season in a row.

The only players to have three-peated at the prestigious event are Ilie Nastase, Ivan Lendl and Djokovic.

Djokovic is the only player to have won the ATP Finals four seasons in a row, which he managed from 2012 to 2015.

The Serb came close to winning five in a row, but was denied by Andy Murray in the title bout of the 2016 ATP Finals.

Jannik Sinner's campaign at last year's ATP Finals

Sinner came into last year's ATP Finals on a dominant winning streak, having won consecutive tournaments in Vienna and Paris.

Remarkably, Sinner had dropped just one set throughout that run, which he conceded in the Vienna Open to Zverev.

In his first match of the group stage, Sinner had little trouble winning 7-5, 6-1 against Felix Auger-Aliassime, who had just reached the US Open semifinals.

He then defeated Zverev fairly comfortably before beating Shelton to make it a clean sweep in the round robin.

Sinner came out on top over Alex de Minaur in the semifinals to set up a final clash with Alcaraz.

Though Alcaraz handed Sinner his biggest test of the tournament, it was not enough to deny the in-form player in front of a home crowd in Turin.

articles.title: Serena Williams once again stands as the only woman in the world to crack history's top 50 highest-paid athletes list
articles.summary: International Sports News: Serena Williams achieves a historic milestone by becoming the only woman in the top 50 highest-paid athletes, showcasing her incredible business acumen and enduring legacy in sports beyond her tennis career.
articles.body: When Serena Williams first announced she was stepping back from professional tennis, in August 2022, she chose her words with unusual care. The announcement arrived through a deeply personal Vogue cover story rather than a press conference, and she specifically rejected the word retirement altogether. She described the shift instead as an 'evolution away from tennis,' a phrase that turned out to be more accurate than most people realized at the time. Rather than fading from public life the way many athletes do once their playing days end, Williams spent the years that followed building out a business portfolio that kept expanding. That portfolio is precisely what has now carried her into territory no other woman in sports has reached.A List Built to Span Generations, Not Just SeasonsSportico's all-time earnings ranking did not always exist in its current form. When the publication first introduced this particular model in 2021, it launched as a much narrower Top 25 list, and Serena Williams was not part of it. She was, however, already recognized separately as the highest-earning female athlete in the world at that point, with career earnings estimated around $480 million. The list itself expanded significantly over the next two years, growing into the full Top 50 structure that exists today, a format that pulls together athletes from wildly different eras and adjusts every dollar for inflation so that a golfer from the 1960s can be meaningfully compared against an NBA star active right now.That expansion is what eventually opened a door for Williams, since the entry threshold for this broader fifty-athlete version settled at roughly $595 million on an inflation-adjusted basis, a bar the retired Formula 1 driver Kimi Räikkönen currently occupies at the very bottom of the list, his career earnings coming to $410 million before any inflation adjustment is applied.The top 50 spans ten sports and athletes from 17 countries, reflecting a truly global mix. Basketball leads with 13 athletes, followed by golf (8), boxing (7), soccer (5), tennis (5), and racing (3), while the remaining nine athletes come from American football, baseball, and other sports. Michael Jordan tops the list thanks to decades of Nike earnings, while Serena Williams remains the only woman to ever make the top 50.The Slow Climb Into a Fifty-Person VaultWilliams first cleared that barrier in the 2023 edition of the ranking, arriving at a tied 49th place with $600 million in inflation-adjusted career earnings, sitting shoulder to shoulder near the bottom of the list alongside boxing legend Manny Pacquiao and longtime NFL quarterback John Elway. The following year brought real movement rather than a modest bump, as capital expansion tied to her venture firm pushed her valuation up by roughly $30 million, lifting her nine full spots to a tied 40th place alongside former heavyweight champion Mike Tyson.By the 2025 edition, Sportico had also re-indexed some of its historical inflation curves across the entire list, nudging her adjusted total to $660 million while she held steady at 40th, now standing alongside multi-sport star Bo Jackson and current NBA guard Russell Westbrook. This year's ranking places her total at $680 million, still at 40th overall, however, positioned comfortably clear of Räikkönen's cutoff mark far below her.The scale of the full 2026 edition puts her position into sharper perspective. Together, the fifty athletes on this year's list have earned a combined $56.2 billion once adjusted for inflation, or roughly $40 billion measured in nominal, non-adjusted terms, through the end of 2025.Sportico has noted that if this same historical tracking were widened into a Top 100 rather than fifty names, the only other women who would even begin approaching that bubble are fellow tennis figures Maria Sharapova and Venus Williams, which underlines just how isolated Serena's position at the top actually is.Twenty-Three Grand Slams, and a Different Kind of Winning AfterOn the court, Williams built numbers that made her financial position among women almost inevitable long before this ranking existed. Her career prize money alone comes to $94.6 million, nearly double the total earned by current world number one Aryna Sabalenka, and that gap reflects just how dominant her playing career actually was across more than two decades of competition.Off the court, endorsements have added more than $400 million on top of that since she turned professional back in 1995, having originally signed with Puma before moving to Nike in 2003, a relationship significant enough that Nike opened an entire building named after her at company headquarters in 2022. Her more recent partnerships have shifted noticeably toward health and wellness following the birth of her two daughters, bringing on glucose sensor brand Lingo, ready-to-eat meal company Factor, and supplement maker Ritual before that particular deal expired. One especially visible recent addition came through Ro, which signed her last year to promote its weight-loss medication, a campaign built around her own account of using GLP-1 treatment after pregnancy, and one that has run heavily in rotation, including a national commercial during this year's Super Bowl.An Empire Built Well Beyond the Baseline DealsBeyond straightforward endorsement checks, Williams has also built genuine ownership positions through Serena Ventures, the investment firm she founded back in 2014, which raised $111 million for its debut fund when that fund was formally announced in 2022. Her personal investment portfolio extends into sports ownership as well, including stakes in the Miami Dolphins, the Toronto Tempo, Angel City FC and the Los Angeles Golf Club, positions that continue generating value regardless of whether she ever steps onto a tennis court again.Public recognition data further helps explain why brands keep lining up regardless of her playing schedule. Recent Q Scores polling, which measures how aware the public is of a given public figure, placed Williams at an awareness rating of 70 percent, a number that puts her in genuinely rarefied company even if it is not the very highest on record. Michael Jordan led all athletes surveyed at 78 percent, a figure that speaks to just how far his fame still reaches more than two decades after he last played professionally. Shaquille O'Neal followed at 75 percent, with Tom Brady and LeBron James both sitting at 73 percent apiece.Tiger Woods matched Williams exactly at that same 70 percent mark, an interesting pairing given that both athletes currently occupy adjacent, unusual positions in their respective sports, present in the public imagination and commercially active despite each having stepped back from regular competition in different ways. Sitting within four points of the highest-scoring athlete in the entire survey, while being the only woman to appear anywhere on Sportico's all-time earnings list.A Comeback That Added to the TotalWhat makes this year's figure particularly notable is that it arrived alongside an unexpected return to competitive tennis. In June, Williams played her first major singles match in four years at Wimbledon, losing a tight three-set contest to Maya Joint. She returned again at the US Open in September, reuniting with her sister Venus for a closely watched women's doubles match that ended in a tiebreaker loss, and pairing with Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles for a run that reached the quarterfinals before ending against Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli. None of those results moved the needle competitively in the way her Grand Slam titles once did, but the renewed spotlight helped push her annual endorsement and speaking revenue to a career high of roughly $40 million, according to Sportico's tracking.In retirement, or evolution, depending on which word she prefers that week, Williams now commands roughly $1 million for a single speaking engagement, a figure that has quietly padded her total earnings as much as any individual endorsement contract on her roster. It is, in a way, the clearest illustration of everything this ranking is actually trying to measure. The prize money stopped growing years ago, the Grand Slam count has been fixed at twenty-three for a while now, and yet the number attached to her name on the ledger keeps climbing regardless, evidence that the business built around Serena Williams was never really tied to how many more matches she had left to win.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Serve and volley is completely fading': Rajeev Ram's blunt take on modern tennis
articles.summary: Tennis News: Bengaluru: Six-time Grand Slam champion across doubles and mixed doubles, Rajeev Ram, 42, called time on his career at the US Open earlier this month..
articles.body: Bengaluru: Six-time Grand Slam champion across doubles and mixed doubles, Rajeev Ram, 42, called time on his career at the US Open earlier this month. The former doubles world No. 1 spoke to TOI about his career, the transition to doubles and the journey that followed. Excerpts...Tennis is a demanding sport. How were you able to keep going until 42?I was always going to play until my body would allow me to do it. More than the sport, the travel got really hard, changing time zones all the time. You have to be in peak physical shape to play. And I found that as I got older, it became harder to do that.How fitting was it to finish your career at the US Open?I don’t think I could have written it better. Maybe if I had won the US Open doubles again, it would have been (great). But to make the semis along with my longtime doubles partner (Salisbury), have my coaches, friends and family there, I don’t think I could have thought of a better way to end my career.Is the art of serve and volley fading?It’s completely fading. The technology, the strings, the rackets, the courts, the balls, nothing is conducive to that style of tennis. Basically, it feels there’s no court, or very few courts and conditions in the world, that are conducive to that style. If it was there, you would see it. You just don’t see it at the top of the game, or at any level.It’s a shame because I think that style really added contrast, which, for me, was the beautiful part of tennis when you had two players playing a different style against each other.Your take on mixed doubles being played a week before the US Open?I was happy with the fact that the US Open is trying to innovate. But I didn’t feel they included enough of the doubles players and people who specialise in that event to warrant it being called a Grand Slam. articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India overcame a major scare before defeating Thailand 3-2 in a dramatic women's team table tennis Round of 16 encounter at the Asian Games 2026 on Tu.
articles.body: India overcame a major scare before defeating Thailand 3-2 in a dramatic women's team table tennis Round of 16 encounter at the Asian Games 2026 on Tuesday. Sreeja Akula held her nerve in the deciding match to send India into the quarterfinals, where they will face North Korea.The tie could hardly have started worse for India. Sreeja was two games ahead against Orawan Paranang but could not finish the job. Paranang fought back to win 7-11, 1-11, 11-9, 11-6, 12-10 and put Thailand in front.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule|Medal TallyYashaswini Ghorpade restored parity with a gritty 3-2 win over Suthasini Sawettabut. After taking the opening game 11-8, Yashaswini lost the next two 5-11, 7-11. She responded strongly, claiming the fourth and fifth games 11-9, 11-9 to make it 1-1.Thailand moved ahead again after Diya Chitale suffered a narrow defeat to Jinnapan Sawettabut. Chitale had a match point at 10-9 in the deciding game, but Jinnapan held her nerve to win 13-11. The Thai player prevailed 11-7, 5-11, 11-7, 11-7, 13-11.With India staring at elimination at 1-2, Yashaswini produced one of the key performances of the tie. She brushed aside Paranang 11-5, 11-8, 11-9 in just 21 minutes to bring India level and force a decider.Sreeja was then entrusted with the responsibility of closing out the contest against Suthasini. She dropped the opening game 9-11 but immediately turned the match around, winning the next two 11-6, 12-10.Suthasini led 8-6 in the fourth game, but Sreeja responded with five points in a row to seize control. She eventually won the game 11-9 and completed a 9-11, 11-6, 12-10, 11-8 victory, sparking India's comeback win.India's campaign also featured mixed results across several disciplines on Tuesday.In boxing, Sakshi Chaudhary advanced after beating the Philippines' Aira Villegas in the women's 51kg Round of 32. India's men's kabaddi team also registered a commanding 63-31 victory over South Korea in Group A.Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Mane finished second in the 10m air rifle mixed team qualification in shooting but ended fourth in the final.In soft tennis, Jay Meena defeated Pakistan's Hussain Arain 4-0 in the men's singles Group D, while Aadhya Tiwari went down 1-4 to Thailand's Alisha Ziegler in the women's singles.Wushu saw Langlentombi Devi Hanjabam finish ninth in the women's Nanquan final. In men's individual foil, Sachin and Hemash Singh both finished fourth in their respective pools.In swimming, Aryan Nehra came fourth in the men's 1500m freestyle final B. India's 4x100m medley relay quartet of Rishabh Das, Akash Mani, Benediction Beniston and Dhanush Suresh finished seventh overall in the heats to qualify for the final.There were setbacks too. Chetan Bhatt lost the men's 84kg kumite bronze medal match, while Alisha Choudhary was beaten 1-6 by Indonesia's Cok Istri Agung Sanistyarani in the women's -55kg Round of 16.India also suffered a 0-3 defeat to Malaysia in the men's Team Regu competition in sepaktakraw. articles.standfirst: La flamante campeona en Sao Paulo llega el miércoles a China con la eliminatoria de la BJK Cup iniciada
articles.summary: La flamante campeona en Sao Paulo llega el miércoles a China con la eliminatoria de la BJK Cup iniciada
articles.body: Kaitlin Quevedo, de tan sólo 20 años, logró el lunes en Sao Paulo su primer título WTA tras derrotar en la final a la argentina Nadia Podoroska. La joven española tuvo poco tiempo de celebración porque le espera la selección nacional de la Billie jean King Cup que juega desde el miércoles en Shenzhen (China) en busca del cetro en la máxima competición por países. El equipo capitaneado por Carla Suárez debuta en los cuartos con Kazajistán a las 17.00 hora local. Esa es más o menos la hora en la que Quevedo calcula poder estar en la ciudad china después de una auténtica odisea. Kaitlin, según ha podido saber MARCA, salió de Sao Paulo a las dos de la madrugada en Brasil. Su primer destino era Doha, la capital de Qatar. Un total de 12 horas y media de trayecto. Desde allí, después de una pequeña escala, tiene que coger otro vuelo hacia Hong Kong. Una vez aterrizada le espera un coche de la organización de la BJK Cup para trasladarla a Shenzhen. En total más de 21 horas y 11 de cambio horario, con el objetivo de ayudar a la 'Armada' femenina. A pesar de su esfuerzo se perderá la serie contra el combinado kazajo. Estará en la grada animando a sus compañeras. En caso de que la selección esté en semifinales estará ya disponible para saltar a la pista si así lo cree oportuno la capitana Carla. Desde que Conchita Martínez lograra su primer entorchado en 1988 son 20 las españolas con trofeo en sus vitrinas para un total de 118 títulos.

articles.title: Kaitlin Quevedo y su dedicatoria más especial: "Va por mi abuelo que falleció en febrero, juego por él"
articles.standfirst: La canaria estrenó su palmarés de títulos en el cemento de Sao Paulo
articles.summary: La canaria estrenó su palmarés de títulos en el cemento de Sao Paulo
articles.body: Kaitlin Quevedo se convirtió en Sao Paulo en la vigésima tenista española desde Conchita Martínez, en 1988, capaz de lograr un título del circuito femenino. La tenista canaria, de tan sólo 20 años, habla con MARCA antes de tomar el primero de los dos vuelos camino a Shenzhen donde le espera la España de Carla Suárez en la Billie Jean King Cup. Pregunta. ¿Es el día más feliz de su vida deportiva? Respuesta. Sí lo es. Siento que este año, he tenido muchos días felices para estar orgullosa. Toda la semana en Sao Paulo fue increíble y todo el trabajo tiene su recompensa. Estoy supercontenta por todo el equipo, por mi familia, porque siempre han estado ahí en los momentos buenos y en los malos, y hay muchas cosas que no se ven en los partidos. Hay muchas cosas detrás y ellos saben todo el esfuerzo y los sacrificios que hemos tenido que hacer. P. ¿A quién le dedica su primer título? R. A mi abuelo, que jugaba a tenis y es por él que empecé a jugar. Falleció en febrero de este año. (Se emociona al responder). P. ¿Qué es lo primero que se le ha pasado por la cabeza tras ganar el último punto? R. Fue como wow, no me lo podía creer porque no me esta sintiendo muy bien en el partido y no estaba yendo de mi lado. Y le pude dar la vuelta. No se me vino nada en concreto a la cabeza. Estuve aguantando y estando ahí todo el rato. Tuve una oportunidad y la aproveché. P. Está rompiendo barreras esta temporada. Primero con su incursión en el 'top100' y ahora estrenando el palmarés. R. El objetivo era acabar 'top100' este año y está conseguido, con mi mejor ranking. Estoy superorgullosa. En lo que queda del año, intentaré disfrutarlo al máximo. Es que eran mis primeros cuartos, mis primeras semifinales, mi primera final, y, además, he ganado el torneo. No podía haber salido mejor P. ¿Sigue jugando con su pulsera solidaria por las enfermedades raras? R. Sí, la tengo siempre y nunca me la quito. Es una inspiración más y es una ayuda para seguir creyendo y para apoyar la causa. P. En París me comentaba que la primera vez que pidió un autógrafo fue a Carla Suárez, canaria como usted, durante su participación en el Miami Open. Y hoy es su capitana en la BJK Cup. R. Sí es algo muy especial. Ya fue especial el poder vivir con ella y con el equipo mi primera eliminatoria en Eslovenia. Carla siempre ha sido un referente tanto para mí como para mi hermana y mi familia. Es una gran jugadora y una gran persona. Siempre que puedo estar con ella y aprender es algo increíble. Es un privilegio compartir equipo. Tengo muchas ganas de estar con el equipo en Shenzhen. Hace días que se lo vengo diciendo a mi entrenador y él me contestaba: 'céntrate en el torneo y ya veremos qué pasa'. Tengo muchas ganas de jugar otra vez por España. P. Me puedo explicar cómo es su vuelo a Shenzhen. R. A las dos de la mañana, tengo un vuelo de 14 horas y media a Doha; luego ocho horas más a Hong Kong, y de allí en coche a Shenzhen, una hora. La eliminatoria contra Kazajistán empieza a las cinco y estaré apoyando en la grada. Tengo muchas ganas de estar ahí y ponerme la ropa con los colores de España. P. Con la ausencia de Elena Rybakina en Kazajistán, ¿hay más opciones de estar en semifinales de la BJK Cup? R. También es una pena que no esté Rybakina porque es la número 1, la campeona del US Open, y hubiera sido super guay poder jugar contra ella. No sé a quién pondrán. La que pongan será igual de difícil porque es muy diferente cuando juegas por tu país. Yo confío en que vamos a sacar la eliminatoria. P. ¿Estará ya disponible para jugar las semifinales si España clasifica? R. Sí, estaré a tope y me da igual si tengo jet lag. Si tengo que estar para animar, lo haré, y si tengo que jugar, jugaré, lo que sea. P. ¿Ha mantenido contacto estos días con el resto de compañeras de la selección? R. No he hablad mucho con ellas porque, cuando estoy en un torneo, estoy centrada en eso. Sé que están todas por ahí y que Cristina llegó un poco más tarde. P. ¿Se puede decir que España es la tapada de la competición? R. Sí. España, una vez en las finales, lo podemos hacer muy bien porque somos un muy buen equipo y hay buena vibra y eso es importante. P. En Roland Garros me decía que su sueño es ser número 1 y ganar Grand Slam. ¿Ese sueño se ve más cerca cuando ganas el primer título? R. No sé. La verdad es que no lo he pensado. Yo intento estar en el momento y no pensar en el futuro porque nunca sabes lo que va a pasar. Ganar un torneo no te asegura nada. Me gusta ir paso a paso, poco a poco y seguir trabajando. No dejar de hacer las cosas básicas. Y tener los pies en el suelo. Es la clave. Pero si crees que algo puede pasar todo es posible. P. De sus mejoras este año, ¿de qué está más orgullosa? R. He madurado mucho como persona, sobre todo la mentalidad por el trabajo que he hecho con mi psicóloga. He estado muchas horas en pista, en el gimnasio, juego un poco más agresiva, yendo a por los puntos, buscando hacer jugadas, soy más completa en general. La calidad de bola... Hay mucho trabajo detrás. Intento disfrutar más, estar en el momento... P. Con el subidón de Sao Paulo, ¿tiene la sensación de que en la Billie Jean King Cup puede ganar a cualquiera? R. Sao Paulo es algo que siempre recordaré, pero la BJK Cup es otra historia. Cambio de mentalidad, cambio de chip y,, cuando vuelva a Barcelona, ya disfrutaré un poco más de todo. Me siento una afortunada de poder jugar las finales con España.

articles.title: España arrancará ante Austria la Final a 8 de la Copa Davis
articles.standfirst: En semifinales le esperaría el ganador de la serie entre Alemania y Gran Bretaña
articles.summary: En semifinales le esperaría el ganador de la serie entre Alemania y Gran Bretaña
articles.body: El equipo español de Copa Davis se medirá a Austria en los cuartos de la Final a 8 que se disputará del 24 al 29 de noviembre de 2026 en Bolonia. El sorteo, celebrado en el Palazzo Pepoli de la ciudad italiana, ha deparado este emparejamiento y el posterior cruce en semifinales con el vencedor del Alemania-Gran Bretaña. Por la otra parte del cuadro, Italia se medirá a Corea del Sur y Canadá a República Checa. El quinteto de David Ferrer, que se metió entre los ocho mejores tras una brillante eliminatoria ante Chile, era uno de los cuatro cabezas de serie en el sorteo. Las asignación de fecha de los partidos quedan pendientes salvo el duelo entre Italia, ganadora de las dos últimas ediciones, que tiene programado su partido de cuartos para el 25 de noviembre a partir de las 16.00 horas. Los otros tres encuentros se jugarán entre el martes 24 de noviembre (16.00 horas) y el jueves 27 (uno a partir de las 10.00 horas y el otro no antes de las 17.00 horas). La Final a 8 pondrá a David Ferrer en la tesitura de elegir entre ocho tenistas a los cinco representantes españoles. Por un lado, están los que jugaron la eliminatoria ante Chile: Rafa Jódar, Dani Mérida, Martín Landaluce, Jaume Munar y Pedro Martínez. A ellos se unirán, Carlos Alcaraz, Alejandro Davidovich y Marcel Granollers que estarán disponibles para Bolonia. Como adelantó MARCA, Alcaraz y Jódar tiene sus plazas seguras, así como Granollers en el dobles. Las ocho selecciones anunciarán sus equipos el 27 de octubre, según anunció la organización. España y Austria se han enfrentado en cinco ocasiones, con un bagaje de 3-2 favorable a los austriacos. En 1933, Austria se impuso por 5-0 a España en Viena; en 1979, España ganó por 1-3 en Viena; en 1990, Austria venció por 2-3 en Barcelona y en 1995, Austria ganó por 4-1 en Viena. El último precedente data de 2012 cuando España se impuso por 4-1 en tierra batida en Castellón y con David Ferrer en la pista. Si España vence a Austria en semifinales le podría esperar la Alemania de Zverev como sucediera hace un año. En aquella ocasión, el equipo capitaneado por David Ferrer se llevó la victoria con los triunfos de Pablo Carreño ante Jan-Lennard Struff y del dobles de Granollers /Martinez contra Krawietz /Puetz, mientras que Zverev se impuso a Jaume Munar. Al sorteo de esta Final a 8, asistieron Angelo Binaghi, presidente de la Federación Italiana de Tenis y Pádel (FITP); Feliciano López, director del torneo Final a 8 de la Copa Davis; Matteo Lepore, alcalde de Bolonia; Roberta Frisoni, concejala de Turismo, Comercio y Deporte de la región de Emilia-Romaña; y el juez árbitro Riccardo Ragazzini.
